title: The Rotomac Loan Fraud
dek: A pen maker borrowed nearly ₹2,919 crore from seven public banks. When lenders feared he might flee like Nirav Modi, the CBI moved first and arrested him before he could.

heroStat.label: loan default including accrued interest, owed to seven public sector banks

promise.quote: Credit facilities extended to Rotomac Global Pvt. Ltd. will be repaid according to sanctioned terms.
promise.madeBy: Rotomac Global Pvt. Ltd., under owner Vikram Kothari
promise.role: Kanpur-based pen and stationery manufacturer; borrower from a seven-bank consortium
promise.context: Bank of Baroda, a member of the lending consortium led by Bank of India, approached the CBI fearing Kothari might flee the country as Nirav Modi and Mehul Choksi had.

target.description: Loan funds used for their disclosed manufacturing purpose and repaid according to sanctioned terms, with the borrower remaining available to Indian investigators.

reality.description: The CBI arrested Vikram Kothari and his son Rahul Kothari on 22 February 2018, booking them over a loan default reported at ₹3,695 crore including accrued interest, against a principal of roughly ₹2,919 crore owed across seven banks: Bank of India (₹754.77 cr), Indian Overseas Bank (₹771.07 cr), Bank of Baroda (₹456.63 cr), Union Bank of India (₹458.95 cr), Allahabad Bank (₹330.68 cr), Oriental Bank of Commerce (₹97.47 cr), and Bank of Maharashtra (₹49.82 cr).

gap.metricLabel: Principal loan amount vs. total default including accrued interest
gap.note: Unlike several fugitive-linked cases on this site, Kothari and his son were arrested in India before they could leave — the gap here reflects interest accrual on default, not asset flight.
